sourceDate.text: 周顯德元年春
天福十二年
隱帝即位
是歲；後漢隱帝乾祐三年冬十一月，赟未至，請太后權臨朝聽政

claims.event: Li issues governing orders after Guo Wei enters the capital and accepts temporary regency pending Liu Yun. Jiuwudaishi 103 s0177-s0185 associates the request with the eleventh-month jichou sequence (day 26); 110 s0184 and Tongjian 289 give day 27. Both are January AD 951 in Julian and proleptic Gregorian calendars; no exact regency day is asserted.

sourceDate.text: 周顯德元年春
高祖微時；及高祖領藩鎮；高祖建義於太原

claims.event: Li was taken as wife during Gaozu's obscure early life, before his provincial commands and his AD 947 imperial founding. This is only a conservative upper bound on that early episode, not a marriage in AD 947.

sourceDate.text: 天福十二年
天福十二年；高祖建義於太原，遂停斂貸之議

claims.event: Gaozu raises his regime at Taiyuan, discusses army largess and accepts Li's advice to stop the levy. This is his own founding action, not activity inferred from his daughter's title.

sourceDate.text: 晉高祖建義
隱帝即位
在位三年，崩時年二十；《舊五代史》卷一百三：乾祐三年十一月乙酉

dateContext.event: Yin's stated age at death is twenty sui. The death is on eleventh-month yiyou, day 22, equivalent to 951-01-02 Julian / 951-01-07 proleptic Gregorian. No birth year is derived.

sourceDate.text: 在位三年，崩時年二十；《舊五代史》卷一百三：乾祐三年十一月乙酉

dateContext.event: Yin dies on eleventh-month yiyou, day 22, equivalent to 951-01-02 Julian / 951-01-07 proleptic Gregorian, although the lunar-year label Qianyou 3 is conventionally AD 950.

sourceDate.text: 隱帝即位
隱帝即位；在位三年；乾祐元年二月辛巳至乾祐三年十一月乙酉

claims.event: Yin's reign runs from the accession attested in 101 s0006-s0007 to the death in 103 s0150-s0152. The Chinese three-year statement counts the three Qianyou year labels; it is not three completed solar years.

sourceDate.text: 隱帝與李業等謀誅楊邠等；《通鑑》乾祐三年十一月乙亥告閻晉卿之前，丙子遂誅

claims.event: Li Ye participates in the plot presented to Li. Tongjian 289 places the final disclosure to Yan Jinqing on yihai (乙亥), eleventh-month day 12, and the murders on bingzi (丙子), day 13. This dates the immediate plotting episode, not every earlier grievance.

claims.assessment: judged elevation of Lady Geng as empress too soon

sourceDate.text: 隱帝與李業等謀誅楊邠等；乾祐三年十一月乙亥告密、丙子誅邠之前

claims.event: Yang Bin is the living target of the immediate plot preceding the eleventh-month day-13 murders. His earlier objections to Geng's elevation and funeral are a separate temporal context.

sourceDate.text: 周太祖即位
南北軍遇於劉子陂；《通鑑》乾祐三年十一月癸未，翌日甲申交戰

claims.event: Guo Wei's army first encounters the imperial army at Liuzipo on guiwei, day 20: 950-12-31 Julian = 951-01-05 proleptic Gregorian. This is the encounter quoted in 104 s0018, not the next day's jia-shen battle. Under a Julian-year convention the old AD 950 was valid.

sourceDate.text: 周太祖即位
是歲；後漢隱帝乾祐三年十一月己丑，奉太后誥迎赟即位

claims.event: Liu Yun is formally selected to succeed, pending arrival. Jiuwudaishi 103 s0177-s0183 gives jichou, eleventh-month day 26, equivalent to 951-01-06 Julian / 951-01-11 proleptic Gregorian. This is selection, not completed accession.

sourceDate.text: 隱帝娶彥成女；《張彥成傳》：漢祖鎮北門，表為行軍司馬，以隱帝娶其女，特見親愛

claims.event: Zhang Yancheng personally serves as marching secretary under Gaozu's pre-imperial northern command. His daughter's marriage explains the favor but does not establish his full lifespan or an AD 948-950 activity interval.

sourceDate.text: 隱帝娶彥成女；《張彥成傳》：漢祖鎮北門，表為行軍司馬，以隱帝娶其女

claims.event: Zhang Yancheng's daughter was already Yin's wife during Gaozu's pre-imperial northern command. The marriage occurred by AD 947; its exact year and lower endpoint are unstated.

sourceDate.text: 夫人卒，隱帝欲以後禮葬，邠又止之；楊邠在乾祐三年十一月十三日被誅之前

dateContext.event: Geng dies before Yang Bin blocks her imperial funeral, therefore before his murder on 950-12-24 Julian / 950-12-29 proleptic Gregorian. This is a one-sided upper bound, not a death in AD 950.

sourceDate.text: 隱帝欲立耿夫人為後，邠以為太速；在隱帝即位之後、夫人卒之前

claims.event: Geng is alive when Yin proposes her elevation to empress. This particular proposal follows his AD 948 accession and precedes her death and Yang Bin's AD 950 murder. The interval does not date the onset or whole duration of imperial favor.

sourceDate.text: 降宋延渥；《宋史》宋偓傳：漢祖在晉陽，遣其子承訓至洛，奉書偓母，與偓結昏

dateContext.event: Yongning's marriage to Song Yanwo occurred by Gaozu's Jinyang phase and before the fourth-month 947 title record that already calls her 宋氏. The fourth-month date belongs to enfeoffment, not the wedding.

sourceDate.text: 天福十二年四月
天福十二年四月封
乾祐二年十二月；《五代會要》作追封，《舊五代史》卷一百二壬午作進封

dateContext.event: Source-qualified Qin title history only, not a settled living or posthumous life event. The title/action fields preserve the cited Huiyao reading, quoted in 104 s0034, with textual-variant certainty; they must not be flattened into an unconditional posthumous fact. The parallel 102 annal reads advancement and dates renwu, month 12 day 13, to 950-01-04 Julian / 950-01-09 proleptic Gregorian. Matching the princess, Qin title, reign-year and month supports identifying the same honor across witnesses. Huiyao itself gives only a month spanning Western 949-950; its exact AD 950 event year is supplied by that explicit match, not by converting every day of the month to 950. The literal posthumous reading conditionally implies death by the honor; Songshi's Song-period maternal context supports the contrary later-life branch. Neither account is selected.

sourceDate.text: 天福十二年四月封；乾祐二年十二月追封；《五代會要》追封（本卷轉引）、《舊五代史》卷一百二進封、《宋史》卷二百四十二宋代隨母歸鎮及來賀長春節

dateContext.event: Actual death date unknown. Only the inclusive lower bound on or after the living Tianfu-12 fourth-month investiture, AD 947, is asserted. This is a contextual life-status inference from her own ordinary contemporary investiture, not an explicit source death date. Death later in 947 remains possible under this limited bound. Huiyao's posthumous reading conditionally implies death by the cross-witness AD 950 honor, whereas Songshi narrates later maternal activity in its Song-period context. Neither account is selected, and no shared upper endpoint, exact death, inferred birth, or continuous activity span is encoded.

sourceConflict.sharedEvidence: 099 s0136 is an ordinary contemporary investiture of the emperor's already-married daughter alongside his sons and nephew, not a funeral list; 104 s0034 identifies the same woman and date. Both conditional chronology branches admit this living AD 947 anchor. Her death cannot precede it, but no common upper terminus follows.
sourceConflict.sourceDependence: 104 s0034 explicitly quotes Wudai huiyao. Its 追封 is transmission of the same account, not an independent second historical vote. The annal and Songshi supply distinct accounts; no numerical vote or intersection of incompatible chronologies is attempted.

witnesses.source: Wudai huiyao, Siku edition, volume 2; quoted in 104 s0034
witnesses.conditionalChronology: If 追封 is read literally as posthumous, death occurred by the honor, not necessarily in its year. Huiyao gives Qianyou 2 month 12, which spans Western 949-950; the matching annal dates the same princess/title/month advancement to AD 950. Even without importing its day, this branch gives only death no later than AD 950. That upper bound is conditional and is not put in the common death container.

witnesses.reading: 永寧公主進封秦國長公主
witnesses.conditionalChronology: Dates advancement in AD 950 but does not itself explicitly date death or say posthumous.

witnesses.source: Songshi 242 s0496-s0502 and the checked web transcription's immediate Song-period context
witnesses.reading: 母漢永甯公主。后幼時隨母入見，周太祖賜冠帔。時偓任華州節度，后隨母歸鎮。孝明后崩，復隨母來賀長春節。
witnesses.conditionalChronology: The retrospective name 周太祖 alone does not prove that the earlier audience followed his accession; its reign placement is contextual, not an explicit date. Independently, the same paragraph narrates maternal accompaniment in the Song period: return to Wo's Huazhou command following the web text's 乾德五年 notice, and a visit for Changchun festival after Xiaoming's death. On the text's natural continuous maternal reference these concern the mother just identified as Han Princess Yongning and support later life incompatible with death by AD 950. No checked passage announces a switch to a stepmother. This remains a source-qualified branch, not an exact maternal event/death year or an assertion that every mother reference must always be biological.

sourceConflict.resolution: No witness selected or emended. Only the independently supported AD 947 lower bound is encoded. The incompatible death-by-honor and later-life implications remain explicitly conditional. Unknown exact death and unselected witness priority do not invalidate this narrower supported assertion.

降宋延渥；《宋史》宋偓傳：漢祖在晉陽，與偓結昏

claims.event: Song Yanwo participates in marriage arrangements with Gaozu's daughter while Gaozu is at Jinyang. The marriage is established by AD 947, not independently dated to the princess's fourth-month title.

sourceDate.text: 隱帝欲立耿夫人為後，邠以為太速；夫人卒，邠又止以后禮葬

claims.event: Yang Bin opposes Geng's proposed imperial elevation and later funeral. These acts follow Yin's AD 948 accession and precede Yang's murder on 950-12-24 Julian / 950-12-29 proleptic Gregorian. The interval bounds uncertainty about these acts, not continuous service throughout every year.

sourceDate.text: 先帝；《舊五代史》卷一百一：乾祐元年正月二十七日，高祖崩，秘不發喪

dateContext.event: Gaozu's death precedes Yin's accession. The exact supplementary primary date is Qianyou 1 month 1 day 27, 948-03-10 Julian / 948-03-15 proleptic Gregorian. No new birth or age is inferred.

translationRepairs: She heard and objected: "Heaven raised us, but so did the people's goodwill; to squeeze their purses before you have eased their lot is no way for a new emperor to show mercy.

The empress heard of it and remonstrated, saying, "From the time Jin Gaozu raised the righteous cause down to our dynasty's rise to fortune, although it came from Heaven's will, it was also because the blessing-power of the land and the people arrived together; to fail to show kindness to the multitude yet wish to strip their wealth is not the way a new Son of Heaven should pity the distressed.

Focus unit names 晉高祖建義 and argues 雖出於天意，亦土地人民福力同致耳; the prior idiomatic invents 'Heaven raised us,' omits Jin Gaozu, and collapses the land-and-people blessing-power claim. The proposed repair restores that remonstrance accurately and completely.
That year they planned to enthrone Liu Yun from Xuzhou; before the boy arrived Guo Wei had the whole bureaucracy memorialize the dowager to hold court as regent, and she assented in edict form.

That year they planned to enthrone Liu Yun, the Xuzhou military commissioner; because the welcoming escort had not yet arrived, Guo Wei led the ministers to memorialize the dowager to hold court temporarily as regent, and she thereupon spoke in edict form.

Focus unit has 徐州節度使赟, 迎奉未至, 權臨朝聽政, and 稱誥; the prior idiomatic invents 'the boy,' softens the Xuzhou commissioner title, and turns the unfinished welcoming escort into a personal arrival. The proposed repair restores those points without introducing new error.
